newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen higher, extends Tues. rise.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen higher, extends Tues. rise.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open sharply higher Wednesday after rallying briefly to new life-of-contract highs yesterday due to strong physical prices and hot weather in parts of the Southwest.
"It's still the hot weather in the Southwest. It's all weather-related," said a New York futures broker when asked about the factor behind the strength in the market.

In over-the-counter activity, June California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were quoted at $17.75-18.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Tuesday's settlement at $17.02, while June Palo Verde (PV) at $23.75-24.00 versus yesterday's close at $23.10.
Third-quarter COB deliveries were assessed at $22.50-22.80 and third-quarter PV at $26.50-27.00.
Hot weather in the interior section of the Southwest as well as ongoing plant outages in the region continued to provide strength in the cash market, market sources said.
More supply of cheap hydropower is expected to move into the Southwest after transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie was increased at midnight.
Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) planned to ramp up transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie to 7,200 megawatts (MW) from 6,250 MW last night.
However, spot hydroelectric supply remained tight as BPA continued to limit next-day sales for peak demand hours. The federal agency has offered little peak day-ahead power since the end of March.
Most of the Southwest was forecast to see dry and warmer-than-normal spring temperatures through next week. The California coast was called to see seasonal readings in the high-60s to low-80s.
A warm, dry weather system was expected to stay over the Northwest into next week with well-above normal readings likely in the southern region.
